Radboudumc
Department of Radiology
Date: 15 January 2025
Exam: Multiparametric MRI prostate
Clinical indication: PSA 7.68 ng/mL, prior negative biopsy, evaluate for focal lesion.
FINDINGS: The prostate measures 80.93 mL. T2-weighted imaging demonstrates a heterogeneous peripheral zone signal. Diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) shows a focal area of restricted diffusion in the left posterolateral peripheral zone, measuring approximately 8 mm in maximal dimension. This area demonstrates corresponding early enhancement on dynamic contrast-enhanced (DCE) sequences. The central gland shows benign-appearing nodular hyperplasia without suspicious focal lesions. No extraprostatic extension or seminal vesicle invasion is identified.
IMPRESSION: Focal lesion in the left posterolateral peripheral zone, PI-RADS 3. Prostate volume 80.93 mL, PSA density 0.1 ng/mL/mL. Clinical stage cT1c. csPCa predicted probability 0.7373852.

previous_notes.author: Dr. T. Hendriks (GP)
previous_notes.text: Patient presented with elevated PSA of 3.8 ng/mL. Digital rectal examination was unremarkable. Discussed the possibility of benign prostatic hyperplasia versus early malignancy. Arranged for multiparametric MRI and transrectal ultrasound-guided prostate biopsy to further evaluate the cause of the PSA elevation. Patient educated on the procedure and potential risks.
